content.0_1_mission:
0.1 Mission Statement & Operational Mandate

Purpose: Standardize investigative excellence across all alert types and business lines to feed accurate, high-fidelity intelligence into the Workstation.

Mission: “Protect the financial system, uphold regulatory integrity, and disrupt illicit finance with clarity, speed, and precision.”

Scope of Coverage: Retail Banking • Brokerage • Correspondent • Wealth • Commercial • Payments • Crypto

Regulatory Frameworks: FFIEC BSA/AML Manual, ACAMS Professional Standards, FinCEN Electronic Filing Instructions, and FATF Typologies.
content.0_2_stats:
0.2 Historical SAR Statistics & Top Typology Trends (2013–2026)

Historical depository institution filing data shows the most frequent triggers necessitating a SAR involve intentional structural obfuscation:

  • Alters or Cancels Transaction to Avoid BSA Recordkeeping Requirement
  • Suspicious Inquiry by Customer Regarding BSA Reporting Requirements
  • Transaction(s) Below BSA Recordkeeping / CTR Threshold ($10,000)
SAR CategoryTrend & Operational Notes
FraudLargest volume driver. Heavy spikes in P2P payment platforms and elder exploitation syndicates.
StructuringPersistent threat. Fragmenting cash/fiat inputs to systematically evade CTR generation.
Crypto/Virtual AssetsScaling rapidly. Heavy exposure to cross-chain hopping and decentralized mixer protocols.
Human TraffickingHigh priority data stream impacting the active Social Harm Index.

content.1_a_universal:
1A. Threat Indicators: Universal Red Flags

Transaction-Based Patterns:

  • Sequential cash-equivalent placements structured just under the $10,000 CTR limit.
  • High velocity 'in-and-out' transactional flows with negligible holding periods or economic utility.
  • Round-dollar transfer anomalies and unexplained high-volume ACH/wire spikes.

Customer Behavior Patterns:

  • Evasive answers regarding source of funds or extreme reluctance to fulfill KYC/CDD mandates.
  • Corporate layering utilizing shell companies or highly opaque, nested corporate structures.
content.1_c_crypto:
1C. Cryptocurrency Layering & Illicit Flow Architecture

Criminal operators leverage virtual asset infrastructure across three defined systemic placement points:

  • Placement: Fiat currency conversion into crypto via P2P physical brokers, high-velocity cash-to-crypto kiosk networks, or prepaid funding sources.
  • Layering: Disguising ownership through privacy-centric mixers, cross-blockchain chain hopping, DeFi liquidity pools, or strategic NFT wash trading loops.
  • Integration: Off-ramping back into standard commercial markets using corporate OTC brokers, physical luxury goods transactions, or conversion to real estate holding accounts.

content.2_1_core:
2.1 Core AML Ingestion Typologies

Directly populates the Workstation's Trending Activity Feed. Mandates case classification across Fraud, Cyber-enabled Crime, Trade-Based Money Laundering (TBML), and Pig-Butchering/Romance scams.
content.2_2_brokerage:
2.2 Brokerage Investigations Protocol

Common Typologies: Market manipulation (pump-and-dump, wash trading), microcap liquidations, and suspicious Automated Customer Account Transfer (ACAT) requests.

Core Logic Pipeline:

Trigger → Profile Check → Security Risk → Funding Review → Identity Review → Cross-Border Review → SAR Decision

content.3_a_payments:
4. Payment Types & Channel Risks (FFIEC)

ACH Matrix: Third-Party Service Providers (TPSPs) batch transactions, inherently obscuring the true originator on the network ledger.

Funds Transfers: High-priority monitoring on Fedwire, SWIFT, Cover Payments (MT 202 COV), and informal networks (Hawala/Hundi).
content.3_b_tiers:
5. Customer-Type Risk Profiles

  • Tier 1 (Universal): Cash-intensive accounts, PEPs, NRA corridors, high-velocity digital rails.
  • Tier 2 (High Priority): NBFIs, Independent ATM operators, professional service provider proxies.
  • Tier 3 (Specialty): Correspondent banking, Trade Finance, Payable-Through Accounts (PTAs).
  • Tier 4 (Wealth/Lending): Opaque trust structures, asset management vehicles, private insurance wrappers.
